title: Compute equilibrium partial pressures via Arrhenius formulas
action: Compute equilibrium partial pressures (atm) of species B, N, BN, B₂N, N₂, N₃, B₂, B₃ at temperatures 2000 K, 2500 K, 3000 K, 3500 K, 4000 K, 4500 K, 5000 K for a B-N mixture at total pressure 1 atm, using the analytical Arrhenius expressions p = p^((y+z)/2) * p0^(1 - (y+z)/2) * A * exp(-T_char / T) with coefficients from the paper's Table 2. Boron condensation is accounted for, so gas-phase composition depends only on temperature and total pressure, not on initial boron fraction. Output a CSV file with one row per temperature.
description: Partial pressures of major gas-phase species in equilibrium for a B-N system.
output_schema: CSV with columns: Temperature_K, p_B_atm, p_N_atm, p_BN_atm, p_B2N_atm, p_N2_atm, p_N3_atm, p_B2_atm, p_B3_atm. All pressures in atm. One row per temperature.

title: Compute boron droplet diameter via agglomeration theory
action: Compute the average boron droplet diameter D (nanometers) using the agglomeration formula from the paper: D = (2 r₀)^(9/5) n₀^(2/5) (2π k (T_nucl + T_end) / m_B)^(1/5) ((T_nucl - T_end) / ℜ₀)^(2/5). Use the following constants: r₀ = 1.2×10⁻¹⁰ m (Wigner-Seitz radius), n₀ = 3×10²² m⁻³ (initial boron atom density), T_nucl = 3200 K (nucleation temperature), T_end = 2800 K (BNNT formation temperature), ℜ₀ = 6×10⁴ K/s (cooling rate), m_B = 1.79×10⁻²⁶ kg (boron atom mass), k = 1.380649×10⁻²³ J/K (Boltzmann constant). Output the result as a single line in a text file.
description: Predicted boron droplet diameter at BNNT formation conditions for the ICP reactor.
output_schema: A single line containing the numeric value of the boron droplet diameter D in nanometers (e.g., '20.0').
